cells in Drosophila imaginal discs make several distinct types of filopodial protrusions, called cytonemes, and that these cytonemes selectively respond to distinct signaling molecules by selectively incorporating specific receptors for these signaling molecules.

cells in wing imaginal discs make cytonemes that respond specifically to Dpp and cells in eye imaginal discs make other cytonemes that specifically respond to Spitz, while cells in tracheal imaginal discs make two types of cytoneme, one that specifically responds to Bnl and another that specifically responds to Dpp.

the role that cytonemes play in signaling in Drosophila imaginal discs.
the mechanisms by which cells communicate with one another.
the mechanisms of cell-cell communication in development, and we have focused on the mechanisms by which morphogen signaling molecules are distributed to their target cells.

cytonemes are a type of filopodium that are specialized to respond to particular signaling pathways.
cytonemes are filopodia that are made by cells to selectively receive signaling proteins from neighboring cells.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
cytonemes are a mechanism of specificity for signaling pathways in Drosophila.
cytonemes are a means of cell-cell communication that is highly specific for particular signaling pathways.

The main takeaway from our work is that
cytonemes are not simply a means to move signaling proteins between cells, but are instead a mechanism by which cells can selectively respond to different types of signaling proteins.
cytonemes are not simply conduits for the transport of morphogen signaling proteins, but rather are specialized to respond to specific signaling pathways.
cytonemes are not general conduits that indiscriminately transfer signaling proteins between cells.
